title: TS SDK: unify streaming ergonomics with AsyncIterator <-> Web Streams interop
creator: Samir Patel
description:
Goal: Provide a robust, ergonomic TypeScript SDK surface for server- and browser-side streaming that lets developers use for-await-of AsyncIterator patterns and seamlessly interoperate with Web Streams (ReadableStream / WritableStream). The feature should cover Node (>=16/18 differences), browser runtimes, and bundlers. It must clarify retry semantics, cancellation behavior, and best-effort resume strategies for network hiccups.

Problems we're solving:
- Many consumers prefer the async iterator "for await (const chunk of stream)" pattern (simple to reason about in server code).
- Browser integrations (and some Node APIs) expect WHATWG ReadableStream compatibility for pipeTo/pipeThrough and composition with other streams (e.g., TransformStream).
- We need clear semantics for cancelation using AbortSignal and a repeatable retry policy for transient errors without double-processing user code.

Proposed API additions (surface):
1) response.streamAsync(): AsyncIterable<string | Uint8Array>  // canonical server-side ergonomic API
2) response.streamWeb(): ReadableStream<Uint8Array>            // convenience wrapper for browser interop
3) utils.asyncIteratorFromWeb(stream: ReadableStream): AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>
4) utils.webStreamFromAsync(asyncIter: AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>): ReadableStream<Uint8Array>
5) response.streamAsync({ signal, retryOptions, onChunk }): AsyncIterable... // optional hooks

Retry semantics suggestion:
- Retries are allowed for idempotent requests only (default: false).
- For a retryable stream we emit checkpoint tokens in-band (X-checkpoint header or JSON event) every N chunks so a retry can ask the server to continue from checkpoint (server support required). For the initial rollout we will not implement auto-resume server-side; instead we provide clear guidance and e2e examples for resumable and non-resumable flows.

Cancelation and backpressure:
- Cancelation derived from AbortSignal passed to stream APIs. Cancelation must cause underlying request to be aborted and propagate an AbortError to the iterator consumer.
- When converting AsyncIterator -> ReadableStream, implement pull() that awaits next() and enqueue; when controller.desiredSize <= 0 we must pause iteration to respect backpressure.

Compatibility & polyfills:
- Node 18+: use globalThis.ReadableStream/TransformStream if present. Node <18: ship a small polyfill and keep it optional; document that consumers targeting older Node should import the polyfill.
- Bundlers: guard against global polyfills leaking into browser bundles.
acceptance_criteria: Provide streamAsync() and streamWeb() helpers in the TS SDK that are exported from the main package
Utilities for converting AsyncIterator <-> ReadableStream are implemented and documented
Cancelation via AbortSignal cancels underlying fetch/xhr and causes iterator return() to be called
Backpressure respected when converting async iterator to a ReadableStream (no unbounded buffering)
Unit + integration tests covering Node (native and polyfilled) and browser environments
A docs page with code examples for: for-await-of consumption, piping to writable streams, and retry guidance
Performance regression <= 5% for common streaming paths (measured against baseline)
decision_log: 2025-02-25: Chose AsyncIterator as canonical public API for server developers because it's the simplest for for-await-of usage and easy to compose with async generators.
2025-02-27: Provide Web Streams helpers rather than make ReadableStream the canonical API — avoids forcing polyfills in Node-heavy workflows.
2025-03-01: Use AbortController as single cancelation primitive across both iterator and stream APIs to keep user code simple and composable.
2025-03-03: Defer full resumable streaming (server-side stateful resume) to a follow-up; initial release will include checkpoint guidance and helper primitives only.
implementation_notes: Implement core conversion helpers in src/streaming/convert.ts and export from index.ts
When building ReadableStream from AsyncIterator, implement a readableStrategy with size predicate to honor desiredSize and yield backpressure
Wrap fetch response.body (web stream) -> async iterator by consuming reader.read() in a try/finally and call reader.releaseLock() on cancel/error
Add an optional onChunk callback that runs user-provided synchronous code and must not block the stream; document that heavy CPU work should be offloaded
Instrument chunk sizes and chunk counts via the logger for early perf comparison; add telemetry hooks to Redwood Console metrics later
testing_plan: Unit tests: convert.asyncToWeb, convert.webToAsync with synthetic async generators and mock ReadableStream controller
Integration: headless browser test (Playwright) to pipe a streamWeb() to a WritableStream and assert bytes received
Node tests: Node 16 with polyfill and Node 18 native stream behavior; run in CI matrix
Abort tests: ensure AbortController abort causes iterator.throw/return as appropriate and no dangling sockets
Retry tests: exercise retryOptions with injected transient error and assert user-level callbacks are not double-invoked for already-consumed chunks
links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-ts/issues/412 -- discussion: async iterator vs web streams canonical API

comments: 2025-02-26 - Samir: Spike completed; produced prototype helpers that convert a fetch ReadableStream to an async generator. Found a Node 16 edge where reader.releaseLock() is a no-op and needed to guard.
2025-02-28 - Dana: Reviewed prototype, requested explicit AbortSignal handling and stronger tests around controller.desiredSize behavior. Assigned to me for next iteration.

2025-03-02 - PR #398 opened: initial implementation of convert.asyncToWeb + convert.webToAsync. CI failing on Node16 matrix due to polyfill import order. https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-ts/pull/398

2025-03-04 - Code review (Julian): Suggested to expose low-level helper namespaced under 'streaming' export to keep top-level SDK surface smaller. Also recommended adding example that shows piping to new WritableStream({ write() { ... } }) in browsers.
2025-03-06 - Dana: Updated tests and docs, changed behavior to call iterator.return() on cancel to allow finally blocks to run in user code. Plan: merge after one more security/compat check.
